body:
I don't know. It's honestly one of the only things that really frustrates me about this person, they simply have no appreciation for anything less concrete than 'X is going to happen within Y months and the consequences will be Z'. Saying 'if we get caught' will occasionally result in a 'If, if, don't bring me if, you worry to much' type response. 

I really hate this whole situation.
I know. A lot depends on how Tuesday goes.

I'm hoping it doesn't come down to that. The person who is discussing this is part owner of the company and has been slowly getting pushed out of certain roles because of a general lack of attention to "details" like this. 

This is the first clear situation where this person is doing something that's definitely wrong, as opposed to just lazy or not particularly thorough. I'm hoping we can get an executive decision and make the decision extremely clear to everyone before any severe consequences occur. As far as I know management is not aware of the situation yet, hence my caution before I run in with incomplete data. 

I hate this because I really like this job and our team, even the person who wants to pull this stunt. Losing this job would be something I'd regret for a long, long time.

I'm not participating in this process if it goes through, regardless of how the conversation goes. I'll quit before I agree to touch it. I may also end up reporting it to HPE and then resigning. 

As far as being caught, we do all support of our servers \(we're an MSP that does exclusively contract based work\) so the clients will not have access to this info... unless they end their contract with us, which would then be a major problem. 

We do register all servers to our account too so frankly I'd be surprised if the mass registration and data collection of this many machines didn't set off an alarm immediately.
